mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a short-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal a softening labor market and disinflation, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are negative despite the described labor and inflation pattern (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% from the prior month predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates strengthening economic demand.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative even when INDPRO shows consistent monthly gains (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and manufacturing activity (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals supply shock, resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive despite two consecutive monthly declines in both HOUST and RSAFS (Rank IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% (UNRATE) and coincides with a rise in consumer spending (GDPC1), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 20-day forward returns due to optimism about job market strength and demand.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and GDPC1 increases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market tightening with strong demand
failure_condition: No significant return advantage in 20 days when both conditions are met (p-value > 0.05 in walk-forward test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as it reflects weakening wage growth and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not statistically negative despite multi-month decline in PAYEMS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% in the prior month combined with rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS) creates a risk-on environment, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% and FEDFUNDS increases in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive return when both triggers are met (Rank IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate a supply-side soft landing, forecasting positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative despite the described dual decline pattern (t-test p > 0.05).
